segments.title: 3 mysteries nobody has solved
segments.say: Three history mysteries nobody has solved. Number one.

segments.title: A book nobody can read
segments.say: There's a six hundred year old book that nobody can read.

segments.title: 240 pages, unknown script
segments.say: Two hundred forty pages, in a script and language found nowhere else.

segments.title: Plants no one can name
segments.say: It's full of drawings, like plants no one can identify.

segments.title: Experts tried. All failed.
segments.say: For over a century, many people have tried to crack it. No one has.

segments.title: It's at Yale today
segments.say: It's the Voynich manuscript, kept at Yale's Beinecke Library since 1969.

segments.title: A whole colony vanished
segments.say: Number two. In 1587, a whole colony vanished. No one knows where.

segments.title: Roanoke Island, 1587
segments.say: English settlers started a colony on Roanoke Island.

segments.title: Three years later: empty
segments.say: The leader, John White, came back about three years later. Everyone was gone.

segments.title: One clue: CROATOAN
segments.say: The only clue: the word Croatoan, carved into a tree.

segments.title: Still unsolved
segments.say: Historians still argue about what happened.

segments.title: A 2,000-year-old computer
segments.say: Number three. Divers found a computer that's two thousand years old.

segments.title: Found in a shipwreck
segments.say: In 1901, sponge divers found it in a Roman-era shipwreck off Greece.

segments.title: Bronze gears inside
segments.say: Inside the corroded block: dozens of tiny bronze gears.

segments.title: It predicted eclipses
segments.say: It modeled the Sun, Moon and planets, and could predict eclipses.

segments.title: Who built it? Unknown
segments.say: Who built it is still not confirmed. It's in a museum in Athens.

segments.title: Quick recap
segments.say: Quick recap: A book nobody can read. A colony that vanished. A 2,000-year-old computer.
